headline: The official same-point comparison with 2022 now covers five states and implies a national vote of about D-0.9 (±1.2) while the polls say D+8.7: by registration, Florida's early vote is D+0.3 against R+4.4 at eight days out in 2022 (Republicans lead the in-person vote by 95,000 ballots, Democrats the mail by 104,000), Nevada is D+5.2 against D+3.0, Colorado D+8.1 against D+3.4, Iowa's absentee pool D+16.5 against D+23.6 and Pennsylvania's mail D+41.8 against D+51.0. Against 2024 the same files pool to about D+5.2 (±1.6): Florida D+0.3 against R+11.5, Nevada D+5.2 against R+5.7, Colorado D+8.1 against D+2.5. The news comparisons lean the same way: Jon Ralston's Nevada count ended the weekend with Democrats up by at least 19,400 ballots, just under 5 points, where they led by 3.1 at this stage in 2022; North Carolina is 36% ahead of 2022 with Republicans a quarter of in-person ballots against nearly a third then; Texas's in-person vote is 55% ahead of 2022 with Democratic and Republican primary voters even; Pennsylvania's and Wisconsin's returns trail 2022.

measures.label: Florida: early voters by registration, D-minus-R margin (mail plus in person)
measures.src: Florida Division of Elections daily file via the app's official comparison, Oct 26
measures.aff: Official data. 2,788,746 ballots through Oct 26 (mail 1,404,356, in person 1,384,390) vs. the state's figures through Oct 28, 2024, eight days out in both years; 2024 is a presidential baseline in which Republicans had moved to in-person voting

measures.label: Nevada: early voters by registration, D-minus-R margin (mail plus in person)
measures.src: Nevada Secretary of State daily turnout file via the app's official comparison, Oct 26
measures.aff: Official data. 395,331 ballots through Oct 26 (mail 238,124, in person 157,207) vs. Ralston's Oct 28, 2024 count at eight days out (700,000 ballots, Republicans up 5.7); 2022 at the same point was D+3.0

measures.label: Colorado: returned ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Colorado Secretary of State daily ballot-return release via the app's official comparison, Oct 24
measures.aff: Official data. 824,754 ballots through Oct 24 vs. the same point in 2024 (interpolated between the state's releases); 2022 at the same point was D+3.4

measures.label: Iowa: absentee ballots received by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Iowa Secretary of State daily absentee report via the app's official comparison, Oct 26
measures.aff: Official data. 91,467 ballots received through Oct 26 vs. the state's report at the same point in 2024 (401,760 ballots); 2022 at the same point was D+23.6, and Iowa Democrats vote absentee far more than Republicans in every year

measures.label: Pennsylvania: returned mail ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Pennsylvania Department of State daily mail-ballot report via the app's official comparison, Oct 26
measures.aff: Official data. 832,250 ballots returned through Oct 26 vs. about 1.43 million at the same point in 2024 (interpolated); no in-person early voting, and the mail pool is lopsidedly Democratic every year (D+51.0 at this point in 2022)

measures.label: Maine: absentee ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Call the Map (Maine Secretary of State absentee file), Oct 25
measures.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated. 174,765 ballots through Oct 22 (Democrats 88,182, Republicans 36,939, unaffiliated 49,644) vs. the same point in 2024; vs. 2022 the gap is D+29.3 against D+29.9 with the count up 40%

measures.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor; Virginia has no party registration, so party is modeled in both years

measures.label: Ohio: early voters by party (last primary ballot), D-minus-R margin
measures.src: News 5 Cleveland, Oct 13 (Ohio Secretary of State data)

compare_note: Registered-party margin among early ballots, 2026 vs. the same point in 2024. Florida, Nevada, Colorado, Iowa and Pennsylvania are computed from the state files by the update job (Florida 2,788,746 ballots through Oct 26 against the state's Oct 28, 2024 figures; Nevada 395,331 against Ralston's 2024 count; Colorado 824,754 through Oct 24; Iowa 91,467 absentees through Oct 26; Pennsylvania 832,250 mail ballots through Oct 26); Maine is Call the Map's reading of the state file (174,765 ballots through Oct 22). Virginia's early voters are 63% Democratic on L2's modeled two-party split, vs. 59% at the same point in 2024 (Morris, Oct 12); Ohio's early voters were 41% Democratic and 28% Republican by last primary ballot as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024 (News 5 Cleveland, from Secretary of State data). Every state with party registration is more Democratic than at this point in 2024, Florida most of all because 2024's Republicans had moved to in-person early voting; against 2022 the official comparison is narrower and mixed (Florida D+0.3 vs. R+4.4, Nevada D+5.2 vs. D+3.0, Colorado D+8.1 vs. D+3.4, Iowa D+16.5 vs. D+23.6, Pennsylvania D+41.8 vs. D+51.0), and North Carolina's comparison is computed from the State Board's files.

bullets.title: The official comparison with 2022 now covers five states and implies a national vote of about D-0.9; against 2024 it reads about D+5.2.
bullets.html: By registration, Florida's Oct 26 file counts 2,788,746 ballots at D+0.3 (mail 604,524 Democrats to 500,692 Republicans; in person 506,708 to 601,357), against R+4.4 at eight days out in 2022, interpolated between the state's Oct 30 (R+3.5 on 2.77 million) and Nov 1 (R+5.4 on 3.30 million) figures that year; Nevada's 395,331 ballots are D+5.2 (mail D+25,607, in person R+5,159) against D+3.0 on the same day in 2022; Colorado's 824,754 returned ballots (Oct 24) are D+8.1 against D+3.4; Iowa's 91,467 absentees are D+16.5 against D+23.6; and Pennsylvania's 832,250 returned mail ballots are D+41.8 against D+51.0. The app's calibrated slopes turn those into +4.0, +1.8, +4.0, -1.6 and -2.0 points of margin and a pooled implied national vote of about D-0.9 (±1.2), against polls at D+8.7 and the app's forecast at D+6.8; the Florida and Nevada 2022 baselines are new, so the pooled figure is not comparable with the D-1.9 reported on Oct 24's three states. Against 2024 the same files read better for Democrats: Florida D+0.3 against R+11.5 (worth about +10.0), Nevada D+5.2 against R+5.7 (+9.2) and Colorado D+8.1 against D+2.5 (+4.8) pool to about D+5.2 (±1.6); Pennsylvania's mail at D+41.8 against D+26.5 is worth about +3.4 (±3.4) and Iowa's D+16.5 against D+2.6 about +3.1 (±3.4). Arizona's county compilation reads D+0.3 on 884,474 ballots with no same-point baseline.
sources: Florida Division of Elections via the app's official comparison, Oct 26
UF Election Lab daily file (Nevada, Oct 26)
Pennsylvania Department of State daily mail-ballot report via the app's official comparison, Oct 26
CBS Miami/News Service of Florida, Oct 31, 2022 (the 2022 Florida baseline)

bullets.title: Nevada: Democrats' lead grew to at least 19,400 ballots over the weekend, just under 5 points.
bullets.html: Jon Ralston's count at 9 p.m. Oct 25: Republicans 'started the weekend with a deficit just under 13,000 ballots and will end it with one of at least 19,400,' a lead of 'just under 5 percentage points' with turnout 'just under 400,000 voters and just under 20 percent,' about 36% of the expected vote. Saturday's close had 375,492 ballots (18% of active voters), Democrats ahead by 16,864 after rising from a 3.8% to a 4.5% share lead during the day; the electorate 39.8% Democrats, 35.3% Republicans, 25% others; Clark 66.4% of ballots, Washoe 19.5%, the rurals 14%. Mail is more than 60% of the vote (about half in 2022) and Democrats win it by about 10 points; Republicans lead the in-person vote by about 4. At this stage in 2022 Democrats led by 3.1 points statewide, and Republicans won that year's Election Day by nearly 50,000 ballots; Ralston projects a Democratic lead of 25,000-30,000 ballots by next weekend and writes that 'a blue wave is starting to form,' while noting voters under 45 are only 16.6% of ballots and Latinos 11.9% against a 15.5% benchmark. The state's Oct 25 file reads D+4.7 against D+3.1 at this point in 2022 and R+5.3 in 2024.
sources: UF Election Lab daily file (Nevada, Oct 25)
bullets.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; county and Secretary of State data

bullets.title: North Carolina's early vote is 36% ahead of 2022; Republicans are a quarter of in-person ballots against nearly a third then.
bullets.html: Michael Bitzer's Day 10 tally: about 1.5 million accepted ballots against 1.1 million on the same day in 2022, a 36% lead he calls 'a fairly stable pattern'; mail is down 35% and in-person up 43%, with in-person voting 96% of ballots; Saturday brought nearly 88,000 ballots against 60,607 in 2022. Republicans are 24% of in-person ballots (up from 20% early in the period) where they were nearly a third at this point in 2022; over a quarter of registered Democrats have voted, 31% of still-registered 2022 voters have, and his Day 9 post put in-person ballots against the same day in 2022 at Republicans +6%, Democrats +54% and unaffiliated +69%. He projects a little under 3 million early ballots by the 3 p.m. Oct 31 close (2.1 million in 2022, 4.4 million in 2024), passing 2022's total on Wednesday or Thursday, and says 'early participation is running well ahead of the last midterm election' while the partisan meaning remains uncertain. Call the Map's reading of the Oct 24 file: 1,544,674 ballots, Democrats 640,474 (up 45% on 2022), Republicans 367,908 (up 4%), unaffiliated 536,292 (up 60%), a D+17.6 gap against D+8.1. The app's own file carries the official comparison.
sources: Call the Map (NC State Board of Elections file), Oct 25
bullets.aff: Nonpartisan academic; official data; Call the Map is an independent tracker

bullets.title: Georgia passed 1.7 million ballots; the AJC finds Harris counties up 9% on 2022 and Trump counties flat.
bullets.html: WTOC counted more than 1.7 million accepted ballots on the Secretary of State's data hub on Oct 25, with turnout about 12% ahead of 2022 as of Oct 20. The AJC's county analysis (Oct 23) put the statewide count about 5% ahead of the same stage in 2022: the 132 counties Trump carried in 2024 are essentially flat, the 27 Harris counties up 9%, Cobb and Gwinnett about 15%, Richmond 65%, while Coffee, Colquitt and Laurens are down double digits; at least 190,000 early voters skipped 2022, and registration is 8.2 million against 7.8 million. A Democratic data firm's analysis reported by the AJC has Black in-person early voting up 33% on the first nine days of 2022 and under-30 turnout up 54%, with the Black share 34% against 32% at the same point (GeorgiaVotes); Rick Jackson's campaign has sounded an alarm over sluggish rural voting. Georgia has no party registration; early voting ends Oct 30.
sources: AJC (Greg Bluestein and Nicole Minshew), Oct 23
bullets.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets; the Black-turnout figures come from an unnamed Democratic data firm

bullets.title: Texas: in-person voting is 55% ahead of 2022's fifth day, and primary-history Democrats and Republicans are even.
bullets.html: TexPolls' compilation of the Secretary of State's reports through Oct 23, day five of twelve: 3,723,684 early ballots (19.6% of 19.0 million registered), 3,534,025 in person, up 55% on 2,276,705 at day five in 2022, when 12.9% of voters had voted in person against 18.6% now; Harris 508,664 (18.5% of its voters vs. 12.7% in 2022), Dallas 315,090 (21.1% vs. 12.3%), Tarrant 260,801, Bexar 239,736, Travis 219,486 (23.2% vs. 15.6%). theoelections' count through Oct 25: 4,251,983 voters, in-person ballots 33.1% from voters with only Democratic primary history and 33.1% only Republican (30.7% neither), the mail 36.2% to 26.5%; in 2022's full early vote the split was 30.0% to 39.0%. KXAN (Oct 24): Democratic-primary voters held an edge of just over 75,000 ballots in a state with about 300,000 more Republican-primary than Democratic-primary voters on the rolls; Republican consultant Derek Ryan said Democrats 'got a huge jump out of the gate on days one and two' and he is 'watching to see if and when Republicans start to show up,' with rural voters needing to be at least a quarter of the vote for Republicans to hold statewide. Texas has no party registration.
sources: TexPolls (Texas Secretary of State reports), Oct 24
bullets.aff: TexPolls and theoelections are independent trackers whose affiliations are not stated; Derek Ryan is a Republican consultant

bullets.title: Florida: Republicans lead the in-person vote by 95,000, Democrats the mail by 103,000; the combined gap is D+0.3.
bullets.html: The Division of Elections' Oct 25 file had 1,402,540 mail ballots returned, 603,510 from Democrats and 500,315 from Republicans (D+103,195), and 1,381,455 in-person ballots, 600,303 Republican to 505,528 Democratic (R+94,775); the combined gap has narrowed from D+6.7 at twenty days out to D+0.3, and the in-person vote is now half the total with every county open since Oct 24. At nine days out in 2022 the state was R+3.5 (1.173 million Republican ballots to about 1.077 million Democratic of 2.77 million), and at the same point in 2024 R+10.9. Political Cortadito's Sunday-morning reading had Democrats and Republicans fewer than 3,000 ballots apart statewide, with Miami-Dade's 263,034 ballots D+9,698 overall and its in-person vote R+4,170.
sources: CBS Miami/News Service of Florida, Oct 31, 2022
bullets.aff: Official data; Political Cortadito is an independent Miami political blog

bullets.title: Turnout without party: Wisconsin's returns trail 2022 by 10.4%, Pennsylvania's mail by 1%; Maine is 40% ahead.
bullets.html: Wisconsin: 317,077 absentee ballots returned as of Oct 22, 36,852 (10.4%) fewer than at the same point in 2022, after 15.6% the day before; in-person absentee ballots are 103,210, up 58.6%, while ballots returned other ways are 213,867, down 26% and down in all 72 counties; Milwaukee is 17.9% below 2022, Dane 20% below, Waukesha 3.9% below and Washington 12.2% above (Dairyland Sentinel, from Elections Commission data). Pennsylvania: 720,648 mail ballots returned through Oct 21 in 66 of 67 counties, 1% below the same point in 2022, with Democrats' returns down 9%, Republicans' up 22% and unaffiliated voters' up 10% (Call the Map); Pluribus News calls it the only state where Democratic turnout trails the same point four years ago. Maine: 174,765 absentee ballots through Oct 22, up 40% on 2022, Democrats up 35%, Republicans 31%, unaffiliated 62%. Michigan's statewide in-person voting opened Oct 24; no first-weekend total has been published.
sources: Dairyland Sentinel (Wisconsin Elections Commission data), Oct 22
bullets.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets and an independent tracker

bullets.title: Nationally, Democrats' early-vote edge looks like 2022's, and the electorate is old.
bullets.html: Pluribus News (Oct 23): more than 22 million ballots had been returned; Michael McDonald's count in the 27 states with party registration was about 46% Democrats to 30% Republicans, and L2's modeled figures 49% to 34%, but L2's Paul Westcott said Democrats had 'the same early-vote edge at this point in 2022.' Nearly 60% of early voters are over 65 and about 11% under 40; 94% voted in 2024 and 82% in 2022. Call the Map's Oct 25 tally: 27,027,006 ballots in 46 states, with the five day-aligned states 10% ahead of 2022 at the same point. The shift from mail to in-person voting continues everywhere: North Carolina's mail is 35% below 2022 and in-person 43% above; Wisconsin's in-person absentee votes are up 58.6% while mailed returns are down 26%; Nevada's mail share is above 60% against about half in 2022; Florida's in-person vote, Republican by 95,000, is now half the total.
bullets.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor whose party figures are modeled in states without registration; Pluribus and the Nevada Independent are nonpartisan outlets

calendar_note: Kentucky's early in-person voting runs Oct 29-31; it is the last battleground opening. Every Florida county has been open since Oct 24, and Michigan's, New York's and New Jersey's statewide sites opened the same day. Closing dates: Maine's no-excuse absentee period Oct 29; Georgia, Texas, Nevada and Arizona Oct 30; North Carolina Oct 31 (3 p.m.); Michigan Nov 1. Pennsylvania's and Ohio's mail-ballot application deadlines are Oct 27. Pennsylvania and New Hampshire have no early in-person voting.
cast_at_note: Ballots counted (UF Election Lab, 49 jurisdictions reporting, state data as of Oct 22-26) when these comparisons were compiled; sets the automatic early-vote weight.
signals_verdict: The official same-point comparison with 2022 (Florida, Nevada, Colorado, Iowa and Pennsylvania) implies a national vote of about D-0.9 (±1.2): Florida is D+0.3 by registration against R+4.4 at eight days out in 2022, Nevada D+5.2 against D+3.0, Colorado D+8.1 against D+3.4, Iowa's absentee pool D+16.5 against D+23.6 and Pennsylvania's mail D+41.8 against D+51.0; against 2024, Florida (D+0.3 vs. R+11.5), Nevada (D+5.2 vs. R+5.7) and Colorado pool to about D+5.2 (±1.6), so the early vote fits a Democratic year without confirming polls at D+8.7. Ralston's Nevada count ended the weekend with Democrats up by at least 19,400 ballots, just under 5 points, North Carolina runs 36% ahead of 2022 with Republicans a quarter of in-person ballots, Texas's in-person vote is 55% ahead of 2022 with primary-history Democrats and Republicans even, while Florida's in-person vote is Republican by 95,000 and Wisconsin's and Pennsylvania's returns trail 2022. The next tests are whether Florida's combined gap turns Republican as in-person voting outpaces the mail this week, Michigan's first in-person totals, Pennsylvania's mail against 2022 and Nevada's final in-person days before early voting closes Oct 30.

signals.title: Nevada Democrats' lead grew to at least 19,400 ballots over the weekend, just under 5 points; 2022's lead at this stage was 3.1
signals.value: Jon Ralston's count, 9 p.m. Oct 25: Republicans 'started the weekend with a deficit just under 13,000 ballots and will end it with one of at least 19,400,' a lead of 'just under 5 percentage points' at 'just under 400,000 voters and just under 20 percent' turnout. Saturday's close: 375,492 ballots, Democrats ahead by 16,864 (a 4.5% share lead, from 3.8% that morning); 39.8% Democrats, 35.3% Republicans, 25% others; Clark 66.4% of ballots, Washoe 19.5%, rurals 14%. Mail is more than 60% of the vote and Democrats win it by about 10 points; Republicans lead in person by about 4. 'A blue wave is starting to form.'
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice. Mail accounts for the whole Democratic edge and Republicans win the in-person vote; Republicans won Election Day 2022 by nearly 50,000 ballots, and Ralston says a repeat 'may not be enough.' Voters under 45 are only 16.6% of ballots and Latinos 11.9% against a 15.5% benchmark. The state's own Oct 26 file reads D+5.2 against D+3.0 at this point in 2022 and R+5.7 in 2024 (the app's official panel).
signals.aff: Nonpartisan outlet (Jon Ralston); county and Secretary of State data

signals.title: North Carolina's early vote is 36% ahead of 2022; Republicans are 24% of in-person ballots against nearly a third then
signals.value: Michael Bitzer's Day 10 tally (Oct 25): about 1.5 million accepted ballots vs. 1.1 million on the same day in 2022, 'a fairly stable pattern'; mail down 35%, in person up 43% (96% of ballots); Saturday nearly 88,000 vs. 60,607 in 2022. Republicans are 24% of in-person ballots, up from 20% early in the period, where they were nearly a third at this point in 2022; over a quarter of registered Democrats have voted; Day 9's in-person count vs. the same day in 2022: Republicans +6%, Democrats +54%, unaffiliated +69%. Call the Map's reading of the Oct 24 file: 1,544,674 ballots, Democrats 640,474 (+45% on 2022), Republicans 367,908 (+4%), unaffiliated 536,292 (+60%), D+17.6 vs. D+8.1.
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice, and much of the Democratic surge is 2022 Election Day voters moving earlier (Bitzer: 31% of still-registered 2022 voters have voted). Republicans' in-person share is rising and they outvoted Democrats on Election Day 2022. Bitzer projects a little under 3 million early ballots, between 2022's 2.1 million and 2024's 4.4 million. The app's own file carries the official comparison.
signals.src: Michael Bitzer (Catawba College), Oct 25; Call the Map, Oct 25
signals.aff: Nonpartisan academic; official data; Call the Map is an independent tracker

signals.title: Georgia passed 1.7 million ballots; Harris counties are 9% ahead of 2022, Trump counties flat
signals.value: More than 1.7 million accepted ballots on the Secretary of State's data hub by Oct 25 (WTOC), with turnout about 12% ahead of 2022 as of Oct 20. The AJC's county analysis (Oct 23) puts the statewide count about 5% ahead of the same stage in 2022: the 132 counties Trump carried in 2024 are essentially flat, the 27 Harris counties up 9%, Cobb and Gwinnett about 15%, Richmond 65%; Coffee, Colquitt and Laurens are down double digits; at least 190,000 early voters skipped 2022. A Democratic data firm's analysis reported by the AJC: Black in-person early voting up 33% on the first nine days of 2022, under-30 turnout up 54%, Black share 34% vs. 32% at the same point.
signals.catch: Georgia has no party registration, so this is turnout and geography, not direction. Registration grew from 7.8 to 8.2 million, which lifts every county. The Black-turnout figures come from an unnamed Democratic-aligned firm; the state's own in-person comparison (+12%) and the AJC's all-ballot one (+5%) differ in basis. Rick Jackson's campaign is warning rural voters to turn out, and early voting ends Oct 30.
signals.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets; one analysis from a Democratic data firm

signals.title: Texas: in-person voting is 55% ahead of 2022's fifth day; primary-history Democrats and Republicans are even
signals.value: TexPolls (Secretary of State reports through Oct 23, day 5 of 12): 3,723,684 early ballots, 3,534,025 in person, up 55% on 2,276,705 at day five in 2022 (18.6% of registered voters vs. 12.9%); Harris 18.5% of its voters vs. 12.7%, Dallas 21.1% vs. 12.3%, Travis 23.2% vs. 15.6%. theoelections through Oct 25: 4,251,983 voters; in-person ballots 33.1% from Democratic-primary-only voters and 33.1% Republican-only (30.7% neither), mail 36.2% to 26.5%; 2022's full early vote was 30.0% to 39.0%. KXAN: Democratic-primary voters ahead by just over 75,000 in a state with about 300,000 more Republican-primary registrants.
signals.catch: No party registration: 'party' is primary history, and the 2022 comparison is to the full early vote, not the same day. Derek Ryan (Republican consultant) says Democrats 'got a huge jump out of the gate' and he is 'watching to see if and when Republicans start to show up'; rural turnout usually arrives late, and the Texas Politics Project found 63% of Democrats but 48% of Republicans planning to vote early.
signals.src: TexPolls, Oct 24; theoelections, Oct 25; KXAN, Oct 24
signals.aff: TexPolls and theoelections are independent trackers whose affiliations are not stated; Derek Ryan is a Republican consultant

signals.title: Florida Republicans lead the in-person vote by 95,000 after a week with every county open; Democrats lead the mail by 103,000
signals.value: Division of Elections file for Oct 25: 1,381,455 in-person ballots, 600,303 Republican, 505,528 Democratic (R+94,775, up from R+50,392 on Oct 22); 1,402,540 mail ballots returned, 603,510 Democratic, 500,315 Republican (D+103,195). The combined gap has narrowed from D+6.7 at twenty days out to D+0.3, and in-person ballots are now half the total. Political Cortadito's Sunday-morning reading: Democrats and Republicans fewer than 3,000 ballots apart statewide.
signals.catch: The same-point comparison still favors Democrats: R+4.4 at eight days out in 2022 and R+11.5 in 2024 on the Oct 26 file (the app's official panel). Republicans won Florida's in-person vote by far more in both years, and the daily in-person margins decide whether the combined count turns Republican this week. Registration is not vote choice.
signals.src: Florida Division of Elections daily file via the app's official comparison, Oct 25; Political Cortadito, Oct 26
signals.aff: Official data; Political Cortadito is an independent Miami political blog

signals.title: Pennsylvania's mail returns trail 2022 by 1%, with Democrats' returns down 9% and Republicans' up 22%
signals.value: Call the Map (Oct 25 reading of the state file through Oct 21): 720,648 mail ballots returned in 66 of 67 counties, 1% below the same point in 2022; Democrats 483,003 (down 9%), Republicans 173,355 (up 22%), unaffiliated 64,290 (up 10%); D+43.0 vs. D+53.2. Pluribus News calls Pennsylvania the only state where Democratic turnout trails the same point four years ago. The state's Oct 26 file: 832,250 returned; the app's official panel reads D+41.8 against D+51.0 at this point in 2022 and D+26.5 in 2024.
signals.catch: Pennsylvania's mail vote is lopsidedly Democratic every year (D+53 at this point in 2022, when Republicans won the national vote), and Democrats are shifting to Election Day voting after their own warnings about the mail; the state has no in-person early voting, so there is no in-person count to offset it. The official comparison is on the app's panel, so this signal is the turnout picture only.
signals.src: Call the Map, Oct 25; Pluribus News, Oct 23
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; Pluribus News is a nonpartisan outlet

signals.title: Wisconsin's absentee returns trail 2022 by 10.4%, with Milwaukee and Dane down about a fifth
signals.value: 317,077 absentee ballots returned as of Oct 22, 36,852 (10.4%) fewer than at the same point in 2022, narrowing from 15.6% the day before (Dairyland Sentinel, from Elections Commission data); in-person absentee ballots 103,210, up 58.6% on 65,078; ballots returned other ways 213,867, down 26% and down in all 72 counties. Milwaukee 46,980 (down 17.9%), Dane 43,149 (down 20%), Waukesha 32,095 (down 3.9%), Washington 9,984 (up 12.2%).
signals.catch: No party registration. Much of the decline is a mode shift away from mail that both parties encouraged, and in-person absentee voting runs through Nov 1, so the gap has been closing by about five points a day. Reporting lags in the state data. The Democratic counties' declines are larger than the suburban Republican counties', which is the part that leans Republican.
signals.src: Dairyland Sentinel (Wisconsin Elections Commission data), Oct 22
signals.aff: Official data via a Wisconsin news site; affiliation not stated

signals.title: Michigan's mail returns are 2% ahead of 2022, requests 17% ahead, so a smaller share is back
signals.value: 789,476 ballots returned as of 7 a.m. Oct 20 vs. 771,967 at the same point in 2022 (up 2.3%), on 2,121,458 requests vs. 1,810,569 (up 17.2%), so 37.2% of requested ballots are back against 42.6% in 2022 (Secretary of State data via MITechNews); the Oct 21 dashboard showed 860,257 absentee ballots returned plus 804 early in-person votes, without a 2022 comparison.
signals.catch: Michigan has no party registration, so this measures turnout, not direction. About 94% of requests come from the permanent mail list, which inflates the request count; returns had been 30% ahead of 2022 on Oct 6 and have since converged. Statewide in-person early voting opens Oct 24.
signals.src: MITechNews (Michigan Secretary of State data), Oct 22
signals.aff: Official data via a nonpartisan outlet

signals.title: Ohio's early electorate has flipped from Republican to Democratic
signals.value: Democrats have returned about 94,000 ballots, unaffiliated voters a little more than 67,000 and Republicans nearly 64,000 (by last primary ballot), per the Ohio Capital Journal from Secretary of State data through Oct 12-13; News 5 Cleveland put Democrats at 41% and Republicans at 28% of nearly 230,000 early votes as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024. In-person votes after one week: 194,841 vs. 50,368 in 2022. On Point Politics counts 764,330 ballots cast through Oct 21 (319,992 mail, 444,338 in person), without party.
signals.catch: 2024 was a presidential year, and Ohio Republicans are shifting from mail to later voting: mail requests are 631,079 vs. 871,041 at this point in 2022. 'Party' is the last primary ballot pulled; seniors are more than half of ballots so far. No newer party breakdown has been published since Oct 15.
signals.src: Ohio Capital Journal (Ohio Secretary of State data), Oct 15; News 5 Cleveland, Oct 13

signals.title: Virginia's early vote is nearly 300,000 ballots ahead of 2022
signals.value: More than 678,000 Virginians had voted by Oct 18, nearly 300,000 more than at the same point in the 2022 midterm (VPAP data via WTVR). Danville has 2,800 vs. a little over 1,000 in 2022.
signals.catch: Virginia has no party registration, so this is turnout, not direction. The count's exact as-of day is not stated. The modeled party lean is in the separate L2 signal.
signals.src: WTVR CBS 6 (Virginia Public Access Project data), Oct 18
signals.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; VPAP is a nonpartisan tracker of state data

signals.title: Maine's absentee vote is 40% ahead of 2022 and 11 points more Democratic than at this point in 2024
signals.value: 174,765 ballots through Oct 22 (Call the Map's reading of the Secretary of State file): Democrats 88,182 (up 35% on 2022), Republicans 36,939 (up 31%), unaffiliated 49,644 (up 62%); a D+29.3 gap vs. D+29.9 at the same point in 2022 and D+17.9 at the same point in 2024.
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice. Against 2022 the gap is half a point narrower, so the Democratic reading comes from turnout and the 2024 comparison, and the unaffiliated voters who decide the Collins race are the fastest-growing group. In-person absentee voting ends Oct 29.
signals.src: Call the Map (Maine Secretary of State absentee file), Oct 25
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated

signals.title: Clark County's mail vote is 7 points less Democratic than at this point in 2022
signals.value: Clark County mail ballots through Oct 23 (Call the Map): 128,824, up 7% on the same point in 2022; Democrats 56,890 (down 5%), Republicans 35,006 (up 15%), unaffiliated 36,927 (up 19%); a D+17.0 gap vs. D+24.2 at the same point in 2022 and D+18.1 in 2024. Ralston has Clark's mail at about 17 points and says Democrats' mail wins 'approach or at times exceed 2-to-1' on the daily files.
signals.catch: Democrats are shifting from mail to in person, which Ralston's county-wide figures absorb; this compares only the mail mode, and mail is more than 60% of the vote this year against about half in 2022. Registration is not vote choice.
signals.src: Call the Map (Clark County mail file), Oct 25
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated

signals.title: L2: Democrats' national early-vote edge is the same as at this point in 2022
signals.value: Pluribus News (Oct 23): more than 22 million ballots returned nationally; Michael McDonald's count in the 27 party-registration states about 46% Democrats to 30% Republicans, L2's modeled figures 49% to 34%, and L2's Paul Westcott says Democrats had 'the same early-vote edge at this point in 2022.' Nearly 60% of early voters are over 65, about 11% under 40; 94% voted in 2024, 82% in 2022.
signals.catch: L2's party is modeled in states without registration, and the 2022 comparison is Westcott's characterization, not a published same-point table. Democrats' 2022 early-vote edge preceded a national vote they lost by about 3 points, which is why the edge alone says little. Call the Map's five day-aligned states are 10% ahead of 2022 in turnout.
signals.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor (modeled party); McDonald is a nonpartisan academic
